title: Written contracts mandatory across the EU agri-food chain — Reg. (EU) 2026/1739 rewrites Article 168 from 19 August 2028
money_note: The regulation attaches no budget to the contract duty; the CAP changes it makes (crisis co-financing at 70 %, up to 6 % of direct-payment envelopes moved to sectoral interventions) are Member-State allocations, not money attached to this need, so nothing is scored.
summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/1739 replaces Article 168 of Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013 so that every delivery of agricultural products (all sectors except milk and sugar, which have their own articles) by farmers, farmers' associations or producer organisations to processors, distributors or retailers must be covered by a written contract agreed in advance and containing a price formula, quantity, quality, duration, payment terms, collection arrangements and force-majeure rules. The duty applies from 19 August 2028 and turns what was a Member-State option into a directly applicable EU obligation.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — Regulation (EU) 2026/1739 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026, published in OJ L on 29 July 2026 (CELLAR: official-journal-act_date_publication 2026-07-29), in force 18 August 2026 (resource_legal_date_entry-into-force 2026-08-18). DATES: 'Article 1, points (3), (4), (7)(d), (9) and (14) shall apply from 19 August 2028' and 'Article 1, point (13) shall apply from 19 August 2029'; point (9) is the new Article 168 (contractual relations, all sectors other than milk and sugar), point (4) the new Article 148 (milk), point (14) the sugar-beet delivery contracts in Annex X, point (3) the new Article 88a optional terms. Transitional Article 4 lets non-conforming products under the new Part Ia of Annex VII designations be sold until stocks run out or 19 August 2032. CONTRACT CONTENT (new Art 168(4)): in advance of delivery; in writing, including electronic form; price static or built from objective indicators reflecting production costs; quantity, quality and timing; duration, with a revision clause the farmer can trigger on contracts longer than 12 months; payment periods; collection arrangements; force majeure. DEROGATION (Art 168(5)(a)): deliveries by a member to its own producer organisation or cooperative are exempt where the statutes set transparent, democratically decided price and payment rules known in advance. Member States may extend the duty to other operators and may make a written offer mandatory (Art 168(2)); they must make voluntary mediation available (Art 168(3)). CARRIED DEBT CLEARED: this CELEX was named unread by the 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-19 reg-scan passes; read today in full via CELEX content negotiation (payload regulation/eu/32026R1739-en.html, 270,928 bytes). DEDUP: no record in the corpus covers agri-food contractual relations — searched all 18,420 signals for 1308/2013, 2026/1739, 'food supply chain', 'written contract', 'producer organisation', 'unfair trading' on 2026-09-21; the nearest records are reg-predkupni-pravo-puda-2028 (farmland pre-emption) and reg-zpf-vynimani-2029 (agricultural land fund), neither of which touches supply contracts. Who must act: Czech farmers and farming cooperatives, producer organisations, food processors and dairies buying non-milk products, wholesalers and grocery chains, and the contract/ERP vendors that would have to issue and archive these contracts; SZIF and ÚKZÚZ on the enforcement side.
quote: by farmers, including farmers’ associations, or by producer organisations or associations of producer organisations, to processors, distributors or retailers, shall be covered by a written contract between the relevant parties.

title: Value chain cap — Reg. (EU) 2026/1560 limits what large reporters may demand from suppliers under 1,000 employees
money_note: No money is attached; the act sets a reporting standard and a ceiling on information requests.
summary: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560, published on 21 September 2026, establishes a voluntary sustainability reporting standard for undertakings that are not themselves in scope of CSRD, and uses it to fix a 'value chain cap': companies subject to Articles 19a and 29a of Directive 2013/34/EU may not require more sustainability information from a value-chain undertaking with under 1,000 employees than the datapoints listed in Annex II. The cap applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 of 3 July 2026, published in the OJ L of 21 September 2026 (CELLAR SPARQL enumeration of publications 2026-09-19..21, file regulation/eu/ojL-pub-2026-09-19_21.json/.rq). DATES: 'This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union' (24 September 2026); 'Article 3 shall apply from the financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027', which is the value-chain cap itself. The voluntary standard in Annex I is usable immediately. MECHANISM: Art 1(1) defines the cap as an upper limit on what Art 19a/29a reporters may require from value-chain undertakings not exceeding an average of 1,000 employees; Art 3(2): 'The value chain cap shall only comprise the datapoints specified in Annex II to this Regulation.' Art 2 lets out-of-scope undertakings report voluntarily against the Annex I standard and use EFRAG's practical guidance. PARENT: Directive (EU) 2026/470 of 24 February 2026 (Omnibus I) re-scoped Articles 19a/29a and simplified reporting from financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027; see the sibling act Reg. (EU) 2026/1563. DEDUP: reg-csrd-post-omnibus mentions a 'VSME standard' in prose as a market note but carries no instrument, no ELI and no date; nothing in the corpus records the cap (searched all signals for VSME, 'value chain cap', 2023/2772, ESRS, 2026/470 on 2026-09-21; zero hits for 2026/470). Why this matters in CZ: the cap is the defence Czech SME suppliers have against ESG questionnaires from German and Czech corporate customers — it makes the demanded dataset finite and public, which is exactly what a supplier-side reporting tool can be built against. Who is affected: Czech SMEs in the value chains of CSRD-scope groups, the large Czech reporters issuing the questionnaires, and ESG data vendors.
quote: ‘value chain cap’ means the upper limit of sustainability information which undertakings subject to Articles 19a and 29a of Directive 2013/34/EU may require from undertakings in their value chain which do not exceed, on their balance sheet date, an average number of 1 000 employees

title: ESRS rewritten — Reg. (EU) 2026/1563 replaces both annexes of the reporting standards for financial years from 2027
money_note: No money is attached; the act replaces reporting standards.
summary: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563, published on 21 September 2026, replaces Annexes I and II of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 with rewritten ESRS that cut the number of datapoints, prioritise quantitative over narrative disclosure, separate mandatory from voluntary datapoints and restate the materiality instructions. The new standards apply to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with an optional-version regime for financial years starting in 2026.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563 of 3 July 2026, published in the OJ L of 21 September 2026 (same CELLAR enumeration as reg-esrs-value-chain-cap-2027; payload regulation/eu/32026R1563-en.html, 2,468,231 bytes). DATES: 'This Regulation shall enter into force on 10 November 2026. It shall apply to the financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027.' TRANSITION (Art 2): for financial years starting between 1 January and 31 December 2026 an undertaking may apply either the old Annex I (2023/2772 as last amended by Del. Reg. (EU) 2025/1416) or the new one, or the old one with eight named reliefs (ESRS 1 paras 27, 32-33, 74-75, 90, 91, 92, 106, 110 — top-down double materiality, undue cost and value-chain limitation, acquisitions and disposals, metrics for non-significant activities, partial value-chain scope, joint operations, Taxonomy disclosures in a separate appendix, executive summary), and must state in the sustainability statement which version it applies. PARENT: Directive (EU) 2026/470 of 24 February 2026 reduced the number of undertakings in scope of Arts 19a/29a and simplified the requirements from financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2027; the Commission departed from EFRAG's advice on 13 listed points, including materiality, anticipated financial effects, GHG emissions, transition plans, microplastics, SVHCs and coherence with Directive (EU) 2024/1760. DEDUP: reg-csrd-post-omnibus records the CSRD scope and the FY2027 cycle but predates and does not name this delegated act, 2023/2772 or 2026/470 (its own note says 'Final Omnibus I text pending formal adoption', which today's payload shows is stale). consult-esas-taxonomy-kpis is the Taxonomy-KPI consultation, a different instrument. Who must act: Czech CSRD-scope undertakings (large banks, utilities, industrial groups and listed issuers) and their auditors, plus the ESG reporting-software vendors that must re-map every datapoint before the FY2027 cycle.
quote: it is necessary to amend the existing sustainability reporting standards by: (i) reducing the number of datapoints; (ii) prioritising quantitative datapoints over narrative text; (iii) further distinguishing between mandatory and voluntary datapoints;

title: EHDS dataset descriptions — Reg. (EU) 2026/2098 makes HealthDCAT-AP metadata compulsory for every health data holder
money_note: No money is attached; the act specifies a metadata format and a compliance date.
summary: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2098, published on 21 September 2026, sets the minimum metadata elements every health data holder must publish to describe its datasets for secondary use under Article 77(4) of the European Health Data Space Regulation (EU) 2025/327, and requires them to be expressed in the Commission's HealthDCAT-AP vocabulary. It applies from 26 March 2029, the date most EHDS secondary-use rules start.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2098 of 18 September 2026, published in the OJ L of 21 September 2026 (CELLAR enumeration 2026-09-19..21; payload regulation/eu/32026R2098-en.html, 32,805 bytes). DATES: in force on the twentieth day following publication (11 October 2026); 'It shall apply from 26 March 2029', matching the EHDS secondary-use application date already recorded in reg-ehds. CONTENT: Art 3 requires health data holders to provide the Part B minimum metadata elements using the definitions, structure, cardinalities and controlled vocabularies of HealthDCAT-AP (Part A and C of the Annex); Art 1(2) extends it to authorised participants in HealthData@EU; Art 1(3) leaves additional voluntary metadata open. SIBLING ACTS published the same day, NOT recorded: Reg. (EU) 2026/2083 on MyHealth@EU (applies 26 March 2027) places its duties on national contact points for digital health and the Commission, i.e. state infrastructure rather than a market duty — its Art 18 grandfathers existing eHDSI contact points; Regs (EU) 2026/2096, 2026/2097 and 2026/2135 concern epidemiological surveillance procedures, the communicable-disease list and African swine fever. DEDUP: reg-ehds carries the EHDS staging dates in the abstract and no implementing act; reg-ez-standardy-2026 is the Czech MZd interoperability standard. Nothing in the corpus names HealthDCAT-AP or Article 77(4) (searched 2026-09-21). Who must act: every Czech health data holder — hospitals and outpatient providers, health insurers, ÚZIS and the national registries, biobanks and research infrastructures — plus the vendors of their clinical and registry systems, who must emit machine-readable dataset catalogues.
quote: The list of the minimum metadata elements that health data holders shall provide for dataset descriptions, and the characteristics of those elements, is set out in Part B of the Annex.
